audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it: Yasuo wins only 47.93% over 2604 games, yet the chart gives Yasuo four stages and Zaahen none. Worse, the two Yasuo-owned early rows were justified entirely by "early Wind Wall denial" — a claim that is false (see point 4), so those rows had no surviving reason at all.
audit.why: Rebalancing four rows on a champion with no mirror audit and no packet ability list would be guesswork. Instead the stage explanations were re-grounded on something that IS true — Steel Tempest's 475 range and Sweeping Blade tempo against a melee bruiser — and the imbalance raised as a question.
audit.corrected: Sides left as-is; whys[1], whys[2] and whys[4] re-grounded on real mechanics. Chart rebalancing flagged for a ruling.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike stage referred to his abilities by invented names and carried no cooldowns.
audit.why: The Darkin Glaive is 10/9/8/7/6s, Aureate Rush 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s, Grim Deliverance 110/95/80s. The 110-second ultimate is the number that makes "drain it with a fake engage" a real plan.
audit.corrected: spikes[0-2].text and mid rewritten with the correct names and the rank-1 cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two fabricated ability names live across seven fields: his E is called "Golden Onslaught" (really Aureate Rush) and his R is called "Final Retribution" (really Grim Deliverance); the Q is written "Q Darkin Glaive" rather than The Darkin Glaive. Separately, the page's entire thesis — Wind Wall denying his kit — is unsupported: no Zaahen ability carries the projectile flag, and Riot's text describes an empowered melee attack (Q), a directional stab-and-pull (W), a dash-and-slice (E) and a downward stab (R). Nothing to block.
audit.why: This is the calibration case for this matchup. A reader holding Wind Wall for a projectile that does not exist loses the trade twice — once to the poke, once to the wasted 25-second cooldown. Three real interactions were absent instead: The Darkin Glaive is an auto-attack reset that heals and can be recast for a knock-up, Aureate Rush deals maximum-health damage so armour misreads it, and Grim Deliverance heals off the damage it deals.
audit.corrected: All fabricated names replaced; the Wind Wall claims in whys[1], whys[2], spikes[0-1], early, mid and wants.you[0] replaced with the range-and-tempo reason that is actually true; anti-heal, the auto-reset tell and the max-health rule written into the do's and don'ts.

audit.why: False positive — Steel Tempest is Yasuo's own Q in the kit file.

edits.after: Level 1 is a farm-off with no committed all-in from either side, then you take charge: at 2 Steel Tempest's 475 range beats The Darkin Glaive, a melee empowered attack he must walk in for, and by 3 your E mobility controls the trade tempo completely - he only touches you when you err.

Level 6 is a mind game: your knockup-into-Last Breath beats him, but Grim Deliverance heals him out of it, so drain the 110s with a fake engage first.

notes: Highest-value correction in this matchup: two invented ability names across seven fields, and a Wind Wall thesis with nothing behind it — none of Zaahen's five abilities carries the projectile flag and Riot's text describes an empowered melee attack, a directional stab-and-pull, a dash-and-slice and a downward stab. The page told the reader to spend a 25-second cooldown on a projectile that does not exist. Also note the passive: Determination stacks into bonus AD and a revive, which nothing on the page mentioned. Chart left untouched pending the question below. Not asserted: whether Wind Wall's terrain component stops Aureate Rush's dash — dash eligibility is not in this data.
